title: Texas Uniform Electronic Transactions Act
rule: Texas's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act covers only transactions where each party agreed, as shown by context and conduct, to deal electronically, and a party may refuse later electronic dealings. There, a record or signature is not denied effect solely because it is electronic, and electronic records and signatures satisfy laws requiring writings and signatures. A signature is attributed to a person if it was that person's act, which a security procedure can help show. The Act does not reach wills, codicils, testamentary trusts or most Uniform Commercial Code transactions. The Act displaces federal E-SIGN as E-SIGN permits.
changeWatch: Amendments to Chapter 322 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code.

sources.title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 322 (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act)
sources.quote: This chapter applies only to transactions between parties each of which has agreed to conduct transactions by electronic means.
